You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: HEAD responses served through http.ServeContent (or with no Content-Length) get a strong ETag computed from the empty body.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.

=== REVIEW FINDINGS ===
- [minor] Compress inside ETag, `Compress(5,"text/plain")(ETag(h))`: the gzip and identity responses get the same ETag (`"532e12b8…"`). RFC 9110 §8.8.3 says a content-coded representation needs its own tag. Reproduced; the 304 to a gzip client using the identity tag is harmless. The tag is computed over the uncompressed body, so it is arguably within "derived from the body".
- [minor] GET with `Content-Length: 5` and no body gets no ETag (`etagServe` with declared length, GET → `ETag=""`). Criterion 2 wants an empty GET body to still get a tag. This is a handler that lies about its length, and `declaresUnwrittenBody` applies to GET as well as HEAD. Reproduced.
- [minor] Headers set after `WriteHeader(200)` are honored under ETag. On a real server with plain chi, `X-Late` is absent; with ETag it is `"1"`. net/http ignores it, so the behavior diverges. Reproduced.
- [minor] HEAD on `ETag(http.FileServer)` returns no ETag while GET does. This is what criterion 6 mandates (HEAD writes no body, so no computed tag), but clients that HEAD first will never see a tag. Reproduced; spec-compliant.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: *, "a"` returns 200. This is malformed per RFC (`*` must stand alone), so the no-match is defensible. Not reproduced as a bug.
